flow: Typed Controls (registry constructors / overlays / verification / planning guidance / reasoning material)

three_question_split.dr1_deliberation: What should CPCS reason about and what knowledge is still needed?
three_question_split.ka1_bridge: How does retrieved knowledge apply to THIS creative intent?
three_question_split.typed_mapping: What canonical representation should the resolved application become?
three_question_split.presentation: How is canonical meaning projected downstream?

affordance_mapping_rule.statement: The TC-2 dispositions (tc2_classify NON_EXECUTABLE_BY_UT / EXECUTABLE_BY_UT) and the DR-1 affordance ledgers (NON_EXECUTABLE_AFFORDANCES, PLANNING_AFFORDANCES) are the inputs that decide CONTROL vs VERIFICATION vs PLANNING vs NON_EXECUTABLE. RepresentationDecision may only cite dispositions and affordances already declared there.

decision_rules.rule1: HARD evidence (Constraint/NegativeConstraint/Invariant/FailureMode) -> CONTROL, plus VERIFICATION when verification obligations exist -> COMPOSITE when both
decision_rules.rule2: verification implications without a registry generation representation -> VERIFICATION
decision_rules.rule3: non-executable evidence classes use DR-1 affordance ledgers: QUERY_STEERING/HYPOTHESIS_GENERATION/CONCEPT_RECOGNITION affordances -> PLANNING (planning_guidance only); otherwise -> NON_EXECUTABLE
decision_rules.rule4: anything else -> CONTROL with target_family from the typed registry

d4: No flat-text evidence admission. Evidence is referenced by ID only in every bridge object (evidence_ids, source_records). Unsupported prose stays explicitly dispositioned and never enters canonical values.

non_executable_objects_policy.statement: Records whose universal type carries a NON_EXECUTABLE_KNOWLEDGE disposition in the TC-2 ledger are reasoning material, never controls. They may emit PLANNING or NON_EXECUTABLE decisions only. A NON_EXECUTABLE universal type must never yield a CONTROL decision.

canonical_score_rule: Resolved canonical scores are never mutated post-resolution (score_id integrity). Planning guidance and reasoning material travel alongside the score, never inside it.
